title: 10. Exercises: OOP Masterclass
summary: SRP-1: Take this UserController class that: validates input, saves to DB, sends email, logs activity, generates PDF report, updates cache. Refactor it so each responsibility is in its own class.
objectives: Solve the OOP Masterclass exercises without looking at the lesson
Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: The 6 Must-Know Design Patterns — SOLID CODING CHALLENGES (5 per principle)
sections.body:
### 🔴 SRP Challenges

**SRP-1:** Take this `UserController` class that: validates input, saves to DB, sends email, logs activity, generates PDF report, updates cache. Refactor it so each responsibility is in its own class. Each class should have ONE reason to change. Show before/after and write separate unit tests for each class.

**SRP-2:** Build an `InvoiceSystem` from scratch using SRP. Classes: `Invoice` (data), `InvoiceCalculator` (tax + discount logic), `InvoiceRepository` (persistence), `InvoicePDFGenerator` (PDF creation), `InvoiceEmailer` (sending), `InvoiceValidator` (validation). Show how changing tax rules only affects `InvoiceCalculator`.

**SRP-3:** Implement a `BlogPost` system with SRP: `BlogPost` (content data), `MarkdownRenderer` (renders content), `SlugGenerator` (URL slug), `PostRepository` (persistence), `PostSearchIndex` (search indexing), `PostNotifier` (notifies subscribers). Write tests showing each class works independently.

**SRP-4:** Design a `PaymentProcessor` split into: `PaymentRequest` (data object), `PaymentValidator` (validates card/amount), `PaymentGatewayClient` (API calls), `PaymentLogger` (audit log), `PaymentReceiptGenerator` (receipt), `RefundHandler` (refund logic). Show how changing the receipt format only requires changing `PaymentReceiptGenerator`.

**SRP-5:** Refactor a `ReportManager` god class into proper SRP components. The god class currently: fetches data from DB, filters/transforms data, formats as HTML/PDF/CSV, sends by email, logs the generation, caches the result. Create 6 focused classes, a `ReportPipeline` orchestrator. Show the orchestrator is the only class that needs changing when the pipeline order changes.

### 🟠 OCP Challenges

**OCP-1:** Build an `ExportPipeline` that is fully OCP-compliant. Start with 3 formats (CSV, JSON, PDF). Show that adding Excel and XML format requires ZERO changes to `ExportPipeline`. Add a `CompressedFormat` decorator that compresses any format's output — again zero changes to pipeline.

**OCP-2:** Design a `DiscountEngine` using OCP. Base discounts: `NoDiscount`, `PercentageDiscount`, `FixedAmountDiscount`. Add without modifying engine: `BuyOneGetOneDiscount`, `MembershipDiscount`, `CouponDiscount`. The engine must apply multiple discounts in a chain — show OCP holds when adding 3 new discount types.

**OCP-3:** Implement a `ValidationFramework` that is OCP-compliant. Core validators: `RequiredValidator`, `LengthValidator`, `TypeValidator`. Add without modification: `EmailValidator`, `PhoneValidator`, `RegexValidator`, `RangeValidator`, `UniqueValidator`. Show adding `ProfanityFilterValidator` requires creating one new class only.

**OCP-4:** Build a `NotificationRouter` using OCP. Routes messages to: `EmailChannel`, `SMSChannel`. Must support adding `PushChannel`, `WhatsAppChannel`, `SlackChannel` with zero changes to `NotificationRouter`. Add a `FilteredChannel` decorator that wraps any channel with content filtering — OCP throughout.

**OCP-5:** Create a `TaxCalculationEngine` with OCP. Current: `IndiaGST`, `USAVAT`. Adding UK VAT, EU VAT, Australia GST, Canada HST must require zero changes to the engine. Tax rules can also be composed (multiple taxes on one product). Show full OCP-compliant extension chain.

### 🟡 LSP Challenges

**LSP-1:** Identify and fix 5 LSP violations in this hierarchy: `Bird → FlyingBird → Eagle/Hawk`, `Bird → NonFlyingBird → Penguin/Ostrich`. Show the wrong design, explain each violation, provide the correct hierarchy using capability interfaces `Flyable`, `Swimmable`, `Runnable`.

**LSP-2:** Build a `Shape` hierarchy that is 100% LSP-compliant: `Circle`, `Rectangle`, `Triangle`, `RegularPolygon`. Write a universal `ShapeCalculator` that uses only the base `Shape` interface. Prove LSP by running all `Shape` tests against every subclass — all must pass.

**LSP-3:** Design a `Collection` hierarchy (`Stack`, `Queue`, `Deque`, `PriorityQueue`) that satisfies LSP. Write `process_collection(collection: BaseCollection)` that works identically for ALL types. Show that each subclass can substitute the base everywhere without breaking behaviour.

**LSP-4:** Implement a `Logger` hierarchy (`ConsoleLogger`, `FileLogger`, `DatabaseLogger`, `CompositeLogger`) that satisfies LSP. Any function accepting `Logger` must work with all implementations. Pay special attention to error handling — each logger must handle errors consistently (no surprise exceptions or silent failures).

**LSP-5:** Build an `AuthProvider` hierarchy (`JWTAuth`, `SessionAuth`, `APIKeyAuth`, `OAuthProvider`). Write integration tests that run the same test suite against all 4 providers — all tests must pass for all providers (demonstrating full LSP compliance). Show what would violate LSP and how you prevented it.

### 🔵 ISP Challenges

**ISP-1:** Redesign a fat `IVehicle` interface into small focused interfaces: `Drivable`, `Flyable`, `Swimmable`, `Refuelable`, `Rechargeable`, `Autonomous`. Apply them correctly to: `Car`, `Boat`, `Airplane`, `Drone`, `AmphibiousVehicle`, `ElectricCar`, `SelfDrivingCar`. Show each class only implements relevant interfaces.

**ISP-2:** Split a god `IRepository` interface into: `Readable`, `Writable`, `Queryable`, `Deletable`, `Countable`, `Pageable`. Build specific repositories: `ReadOnlyCache(Readable, Countable)`, `AppendLog(Writable)`, `FullRepository(all interfaces)`, `SearchIndex(Queryable, Countable)`. Write service classes that depend only on the minimal interface they need.

**ISP-3:** Design a messaging system with ISP. Fat interface: `IMessenger`. Split into: `Sendable`, `Receivable`, `Schedulable`, `Trackable`, `Cancellable`, `Broadcastable`. Build: `SMSService(Sendable, Trackable)`, `EmailService(Sendable, Receivable, Schedulable, Trackable, Cancellable)`, `PushService(Sendable, Broadcastable)`. Show how adding `Retryable` affects only relevant services.

**ISP-4:** Refactor a `IUserService` fat interface (20 methods) into role-based thin interfaces: `UserReader`, `UserWriter`, `UserAuthenticator`, `UserAuthorizer`, `UserProfileManager`, `UserNotifier`. Different controllers depend only on what they need: `LoginController(UserReader, UserAuthenticator)`, `ProfileController(UserReader, UserProfileManager)`, `AdminController(UserReader, UserWriter, UserAuthorizer)`.

**ISP-5:** Build a `DataPipeline` with ISP-compliant stages: `Extractable`, `Transformable`, `Loadable`, `Validatable`, `Loggable`, `Monitorable`. Compose specific pipelines: `SimpleETL(Extractable, Transformable, Loadable)`, `ValidatedETL(+ Validatable)`, `MonitoredETL(+ Loggable, Monitorable)`. Show adding monitoring to an existing pipeline requires only implementing `Monitorable` — nothing else changes.

### 🟣 DIP Challenges

**DIP-1:** Refactor a `ReportService` that directly instantiates `MySQLDatabase`, `GmailEmailer`, `LocalFileStorage`, `ConsoleLogger`. Apply DIP to make all 4 dependencies injectable. Show the same `ReportService` working with: Production config (MySQL + Gmail + S3 + CloudWatch) and Test config (InMemory + MockEmail + InMemory + Silent).

**DIP-2:** Build a complete `EcommerceCheckout` using DIP: `CheckoutService` depends on: `PaymentGateway`, `InventoryService`, `OrderRepository`, `NotificationService`, `TaxCalculator`, `ShippingCalculator`. Wire up 3 different configurations: India, USA, Test. Show `CheckoutService` code never changes across configurations.

**DIP-3:** Design a plugin-based architecture using DIP. `ApplicationCore` depends on: `DataSource`, `BusinessRuleEngine`, `OutputFormatter`, `AuditLogger`. Each can have 3+ implementations. Build a `Container` class that wires dependencies based on a config dict. Show adding a new `MongoDBDataSource` requires zero changes to `ApplicationCore`.

**DIP-4:** Implement a microservices-style `OrderFulfillmentService` using DIP. Dependencies: `InventoryClient`, `PaymentClient`, `ShippingClient`, `NotificationClient`. For each: production implementation (HTTP client), test implementation (mock), development implementation (fake with delays). Show full DIP compliance with a simple DI container.

**DIP-5:** Create a `DataSyncService` that synchronizes data between systems. Depends on: `SourceRepository`, `DestinationRepository`, `TransformationEngine`, `ConflictResolver`, `SyncLogger`. Build 5 different sync configurations by mixing different implementations. Show the sync logic (business rules) is completely isolated from all infrastructure concerns.

sections.title: The 6 Must-Know Design Patterns — DESIGN PATTERN CODING CHALLENGES (5 per pattern)
sections.body:
### 🔵 Singleton Challenges

**S-1:** Implement a thread-safe `ConnectionPool` Singleton with: `get_connection()`, `release_connection()`, `get_stats()`, `reset()` (for testing). Pool should manage up to N connections. Show thread safety with 50 concurrent threads each requesting connections. Verify exactly ONE pool exists regardless of concurrent creation attempts.

**S-2:** Build a `ConfigurationManager` Singleton that: loads from YAML/JSON/ENV, supports hot-reload (reloads config without restart), notifies registered callbacks when config changes, is thread-safe. Prove it's a singleton across 10 modules all importing it.

**S-3:** Implement a `CacheManager` Singleton with: TTL support, LRU eviction, thread-safe get/set/delete, cache statistics (hits, misses, evictions). Add a `@cached(ttl=60)` decorator that uses the singleton cache. Show cache is shared across all modules.

**S-4:** Design a `AuditLogger` Singleton for compliance logging: buffered writes (batch to DB every N seconds), thread-safe, supports log levels, guaranteed delivery (no loss on shutdown), searchable log history. Write tests that verify ONE logger exists, and all modules write to the same audit trail.

**S-5:** Create a `FeatureFlags` Singleton that: loads flags from a remote source, caches with TTL, supports A/B testing (percentage rollout), provides `@feature_flag('flag_name')` decorator. Demonstrate that ALL code using feature flags reads from ONE shared instance, and changing a flag value is immediately visible everywhere.

### 🟢 Factory Challenges

**F-1:** Build a `DatabaseFactory` that creates: `MySQLDatabase`, `PostgreSQLDatabase`, `SQLiteDatabase`, `MongoDatabase` — selected by config/environment. Factory must also handle connection pooling, retry logic, and health checks. Show adding `RedisDatabase` requires only one new class + factory registration.

**F-2:** Implement an `AbstractNotificationFactory` for a multi-region app: `IndiaFactory`, `USAFactory`, `EUFactory`. Each factory creates region-appropriate: transactional notification, marketing notification, OTP notification. Show how adding `BrazilFactory` requires only one new factory class.

**F-3:** Design a `UIComponentFactory` for a cross-platform app: `WebFactory`, `MobileFactory`, `DesktopFactory`. Each creates platform-specific: `Button`, `TextInput`, `Modal`, `DataGrid`. Show that application code uses only abstract component types — it works across all platforms without `isinstance` checks.

**F-4:** Build a `PaymentMethodFactory` that creates: `CreditCardPayment`, `UPIPayment`, `NetBankingPayment`, `WalletPayment`, `CryptoPayment`. Factory validates user eligibility for each method. Add caching — same payment method instance reused per session. Show zero business logic changes when adding `BNPLPayment`.

**F-5:** Create a `ReportFactory` with a registration system: any new report type self-registers using a class decorator. Factory can then create it by string name. Build: `SalesReport`, `InventoryReport`, `CustomerReport`, `FinancialReport`. Show how a third-party plugin can add `CustomReport` that auto-registers with the factory.

### 🟠 Decorator Pattern Challenges

**D-1:** Build a `QueryBuilder` with decorators: `CachingDecorator` (cache query results), `LoggingDecorator` (log query + time), `RetryDecorator` (retry on failure), `TimeoutDecorator` (cancel if too slow), `MetricsDecorator` (count/time all queries). Stack them in 3 different configurations and show each adds its behaviour independently.

**D-2:** Design an `APIClient` using Decorator Pattern: base client makes HTTP requests. Add: `AuthDecorator` (adds JWT), `RetryDecorator` (retries on 5xx), `RateLimitDecorator` (throttles requests), `CachingDecorator` (caches GETs), `LoggingDecorator` (logs request/response). Show runtime composition of different client configurations for different API endpoints.

**D-3:** Implement a `TextProcessor` decorator chain: base processes raw text. Add decorators: `SpellCheckDecorator`, `GrammarDecorator`, `SentimentDecorator`, `TranslationDecorator`, `SummaryDecorator`. Each can be added/removed independently. Show the same text processed through 5 different decorator combinations producing different results.

**D-4:** Build a `FileHandler` decorator system: `EncryptionDecorator` (AES encrypt/decrypt), `CompressionDecorator` (gzip), `ChecksumDecorator` (MD5 verification), `VersioningDecorator` (keeps versions), `BackupDecorator` (auto-backup on write). Stack them for a secure file storage pipeline. Verify data integrity end-to-end.

**D-5:** Create an `EventHandler` decorator chain for a web framework: `AuthenticationDecorator`, `AuthorizationDecorator`, `ValidationDecorator`, `RateLimitDecorator`, `LoggingDecorator`, `MetricsDecorator`. Build a DSL: `handler = build_handler(MyHandler, auth=True, rate_limit=100, log=True)`. Show how different endpoints get different decorator combinations.

### 🔴 Observer Challenges

**O-1:** Build a complete `StockMarket` Observer system: `StockMarket` emits price change events. Observers: `PriceAlertObserver` (triggers when price crosses threshold), `TradingBotObserver` (auto-buy/sell), `PortfolioTrackerObserver` (updates portfolio value), `NewsPublisherObserver` (publishes news on big moves), `ChartObserver` (updates price chart). Show 20 price changes triggering appropriate observers.

**O-2:** Implement a `GameEventSystem` using Observer: `GameWorld` emits events. Observers: `UIObserver` (updates health/score display), `SoundObserver` (plays sounds on events), `AchievementObserver` (unlocks achievements), `SaveGameObserver` (auto-saves on key events), `NetworkObserver` (syncs multiplayer). Show a full game session with 15 events flowing through all observers.

**O-3:** Design a `CI/CD Pipeline` event system: `Pipeline` emits: build_started, build_passed, build_failed, tests_passed, tests_failed, deployed, rollback. Observers: `SlackNotifier`, `EmailNotifier`, `JiraTicketCreator`, `MetricsCollector`, `AutoRollbackTrigger`, `DeveloperPager`. Show a full pipeline run with success and failure scenarios.

**O-4:** Create a `SmartHome` Observer system: `Home` emits: motion_detected, door_opened, temperature_changed, power_outage, smoke_detected. Observers: `SecuritySystem`, `LightingController`, `HVACController`, `AlertSender`, `LoggingSystem`, `AutomationEngine`. Show cascading events (smoke → alert → call fire dept → unlock doors → notify family).

**O-5:** Build a `DataStreamProcessor` using Observer: `DataStream` pushes real-time data. Observers: `AnomalyDetector` (detects outliers), `Aggregator` (rolling averages), `Alerter` (threshold alerts), `DataStore` (persists to DB), `Dashboard` (real-time display). Add `FilteredObserver` wrapper — only receives events matching a predicate. Simulate 1000 events flowing through the system.

### 🟡 Strategy Challenges

**S-1:** Build a complete `SortingService` with strategies: `BubbleSort`, `QuickSort`, `MergeSort`, `HeapSort`, `TimSort`. Add `AdaptiveStrategy` that automatically picks the best algorithm based on data size and type. Benchmark all strategies on various datasets. Show the service never changes when new sort algorithms are added.

**S-2:** Design a `AuthenticationService` with strategies: `PasswordAuth`, `JWTAuth`, `OAuthAuth`, `BiometricAuth`, `TwoFactorAuth`. Each strategy handles: authenticate, validate_token, refresh. Build a `MultiFactorStrategy` that chains two strategies. Show zero changes to `AuthController` when switching or combining strategies.

**S-3:** Implement a `ImageProcessingPipeline` with strategies for each stage: Resize (`AspectRatioResize`, `CropResize`, `FitResize`), Filter (`GrayscaleFilter`, `BlurFilter`, `SharpenFilter`), Compression (`JPEGCompressor`, `PNGCompressor`, `WebPCompressor`). Build pipelines for: thumbnail generation, profile photo, high-quality archive. Zero code change in pipeline when adding `AVIFCompressor`.

**S-4:** Build a `RecommendationEngine` with strategies: `CollaborativeFiltering`, `ContentBasedFiltering`, `PopularityBasedFiltering`, `HybridStrategy` (combines multiple). `HybridStrategy` accepts a list of strategies with weights and merges their recommendations. Show adding `MLModelStrategy` requires no changes to the recommendation service.

**S-5:** Create a `BackupStrategy` system: `FullBackup` (complete), `IncrementalBackup` (changes since last), `DifferentialBackup` (changes since last full). Add strategies for storage: `LocalStorage`, `S3Storage`, `GDriveStorage`. Compose them: `BackupJob(IncrementalBackup(), S3Storage())`. Show any combination works — 3 backup types × 3 storages = 9 combinations, zero new code in BackupJob.

### 🟣 Repository Challenges

**R-1:** Implement a complete `BookLibrary` system using Repository Pattern: `BookRepository`, `MemberRepository`, `LoanRepository`. Business logic in `LibraryService` (borrow, return, reserve, search). Build InMemory + SQLite implementations for each repository. Run the same integration tests against both — identical results prove Repository Pattern abstraction works.

**R-2:** Design a `HospitalManagement` Repository system: `PatientRepository`, `DoctorRepository`, `AppointmentRepository`, `PrescriptionRepository`. `HospitalService` orchestrates: book appointment, write prescription, discharge patient. Use Repository pattern to ensure all business logic is DB-agnostic. Show switching from MySQL to MongoDB requires only new repository implementations.

**R-3:** Build a `ECommerceRepository` system with Unit of Work pattern: multiple repositories participate in ONE transaction. `UnitOfWork` manages: `OrderRepository`, `InventoryRepository`, `PaymentRepository`. If payment fails → order and inventory changes auto-rollback. Show atomic multi-repo operations using InMemory implementation.

**R-4:** Implement a `CachingRepository` decorator: wraps any `Repository` implementation, caches reads with TTL, invalidates cache on writes. Apply to `ProductRepository` — reads served from cache, writes go to DB and invalidate cache. Show: 10 reads (9 cached, 1 DB hit), 1 write (DB + cache invalidation), 10 more reads (1 DB hit, 9 cached).

**R-5:** Design a `FederatedRepository` that merges data from multiple sources: `LocalRepository` (fast, limited), `RemoteAPIRepository` (slow, complete), `CacheRepository` (fastest, may be stale). `FederatedProductRepository` tries local first, then cache, then remote. Aggregates and deduplicates results. Show transparent multi-source data access behind one repository interface.

# 🗺️ COMPLETE COURSE PROGRESS

sections.title: The 6 Must-Know Design Patterns — DDD CODING CHALLENGES
sections.body:
**DDD-1:** Build a complete `BankingDomain` using DDD. Aggregates: `Account` (balance, transactions), `Customer` (KYC, accounts). Value Objects: `Money`, `IBAN`, `TransactionId`, `KYCStatus`. Domain Events: `AccountOpened`, `MoneyDeposited`, `MoneyWithdrawn`, `TransferInitiated`, `TransferCompleted`. Domain Service: `MoneyTransferService` (coordinates two Account aggregates). Invariant: cannot overdraw, cannot transfer to self. Show full transfer flow with event dispatch.

**DDD-2:** Design a `HospitalDomain`. Aggregates: `Patient` (medical history, allergies), `Doctor` (schedule, specialization), `Appointment` (status, diagnosis). Value Objects: `PatientId`, `Diagnosis`, `Prescription`, `TimeSlot`. Domain Events: `AppointmentBooked`, `AppointmentCancelled`, `DiagnosisRecorded`, `PrescriptionIssued`. Domain Service: `AppointmentBookingService`. Invariants: doctor cannot have overlapping appointments, patient cannot book same doctor twice same day. Full booking + diagnosis + prescription flow.

**DDD-3:** Create a `HotelBookingDomain`. Aggregates: `Room` (availability, pricing), `Booking` (guest, dates, addons), `Guest` (profile, loyalty points). Value Objects: `DateRange`, `RoomType`, `Money`, `LoyaltyPoints`. Domain Events: `BookingCreated`, `BookingConfirmed`, `BookingCancelled`, `CheckedIn`, `CheckedOut`, `LoyaltyPointsEarned`. Domain Service: `BookingService`. Invariants: no double booking, cancellation within 24h is free, loyalty points calculated on checkout. Full lifecycle.

**DDD-4:** Implement a `LibraryDomain`. Aggregates: `Book` (copies, availability), `Member` (borrowing history, fines), `Loan` (book, member, due date). Value Objects: `ISBN`, `CopyId`, `LoanPeriod`, `Fine`. Domain Events: `BookBorrowed`, `BookReturned`, `FineAccrued`, `FinePaid`, `BookReserved`. Domain Service: `LoanManagementService`. Invariants: max 3 books per member, fine ₹10/day overdue, reserved books held 48h. Show full borrow → overdue → fine → return → pay fine flow.

**DDD-5:** Build a complete `FlightBookingDomain`. Aggregates: `Flight` (seats, pricing tiers), `Booking` (passengers, seats), `Passenger` (frequent flyer). Value Objects: `SeatNumber`, `FlightNumber`, `PNR`, `Money`, `FrequentFlyerMiles`. Domain Events: `BookingCreated`, `SeatAssigned`, `BookingCancelled`, `FlightDelayed`, `MilesEarned`. Domain Service: `BookingService` (handles seat selection, passenger assignment). Invariants: cannot book full flight, refund rules by fare class, miles earned only on completed flights. Full 3-passenger booking + cancellation + rebooking flow.
